Loewner order.d: A way to compare two symmetric matrices. A ⪰ B means A − B is positive semidefinite, so vᵀAv ≥ vᵀBv for every direction v. Like saying room A is at least as warm as room B at every single spot, not just on average.

Weyl monotonicity.d: If A ⪰ B (A − B is positive semidefinite), then each eigenvalue of A, sorted from largest, is at least the matching sorted eigenvalue of B. It says nothing about whether the eigenvectors agree.

Courant–Fischer theorem.d: The i-th largest eigenvalue of a symmetric matrix A equals the largest value, over all i-dimensional subspaces U, of the smallest vᵀAv for unit v in U. It turns eigenvalue questions into questions about quadratic forms.

equivariant.d: A procedure is equivariant to a transformation if transforming the input transforms the output in the matching way. Example: flip a photo left to right, then find its brightest spot; you get the flipped spot.

conjugation.d: For matrices, conjugating H by an orthogonal D means forming D H Dᵀ (here D H D, because the sign-flip matrices are their own inverse). It is the same curvature written after the axes have been flipped or rotated.

GOE.d: A random symmetric matrix whose entries (up to symmetry) are independent Gaussians. Its law does not change under any rotation of the axes, so it has no preferred direction: a model of structureless curvature.

exchangeable.d: A list of random quantities is exchangeable if shuffling the list does not change their joint law. Example: the values on five lottery balls, listed in the order they were drawn.

geometric mean.d: Average the logarithms, then map back with exp. For 2 and 8 it is √(2 × 8) = 4. It stops a few huge ratios from dominating an average of ratios.

trunk.d: The body of the network up to the last layer's residual state, before the final norm and softmax. A trunk interaction is already present in that state; it is not created by the final normalisation and softmax.

token class.d: A coarse label for a token by its characters: digit (only digits), punctuation (no letters or digits), whitespace/newline (empty after trimming), or word (anything else). Run 2 used it to see which kinds of tokens carry curvature energy.

wikitext-103.d: A public corpus of Wikipedia articles with train, validation and test splits. Every H-space run drew its text windows from it.

multiple comparisons.d: Running many tests raises the chance that one passes by luck, especially when a later test is chosen after looking at earlier data. Counting the tests in a sequence keeps this risk visible.

retention score.d: How much of the interaction (r_I) or of the main effects (r_M) survives an ablation, as an energy-weighted ratio; 1 means nothing was removed. The specificity S = r_M − r_I is positive when the ablation removes interactions more than main effects.

spectral gap.d: The difference (or ratio) between consecutive sorted eigenvalues, for example λ₂₅ versus λ₂₆. A small gap means the top-k eigenspace is poorly defined: tiny noise can swap directions across the cut.

pre-norm proxy.d: The quantity u_t · h_L* = rms(h_L*) · logit_t that the J-lens and the H-lens differentiate: the final residual read along a token's unembedding direction before the final RMSNorm. It is not the logit itself.

mean-ablation.d: Replacing the part of an activation that lies in a subspace by its average value over the data, so the subspace stops carrying information about the current input.
